pairs: In diebus illis ægrotavit Ezechias usque ad mortem;
In those days Hezekiah became ill and was near death. And so,
Isaiah, the son of Amoz, the prophet,
quia morieris tu, et non vives.
for you shall die, and you shall not live.”
Et convertit Ezechias faciem suam ad parietem,
And Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall,
and he prayed to the Lord.
to remember how I walked before you in truth
quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et in corde perfecto,
et quod bonum est in oculis tuis fecerim.
and that I have done what is good in your sight.”
And Hezekiah wept with a great weeping.
Et factum est verbum Domini ad Isaiam,
And the word of the Lord came to Isaiah,
Hæc dicit Dominus Deus David patris tui:
Thus says the Lord, the God of David, your father:
and I have seen your tears.
ecce ego adjiciam super dies tuos quindecim annos,
Behold, I will add fifteen years to your days.
et de manu regis Assyriorum eruam te,
and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians,
Hoc autem tibi erit signum a Domino,
And this will be a sign for you from the Lord,
quia faciet Dominus verbum hoc quod locutus est:
that the Lord will do this word, which he has spoken:
ecce ego reverti faciam umbram linearum per quas descenderat in horologio Achaz in sole,
Behold, I will cause the shadow of the lines, which has now descended on the sundial of Ahaz,
to move in reverse for ten lines.”
Et reversus est sol decem lineis per gradus quos descenderat.
And so, the sun moved backward by ten lines, through the degrees by which it had descended.
cum ægrotasset et convaluisset de infirmitate sua.
after he had fallen ill and had recovered from his sickness:
Ego dixi in dimidio dierum meorum:
“I said: In the middle of my days,
I will go to the gates of Hell.
So I sought the remainder of my years.
Non videbo Dominum Deum in terra viventium;
I will not see the Lord God in the land of the living.
I will no longer behold man,
My longevity has been taken away;
et convoluta est a me, quasi tabernaculum pastorum.
it has been folded up and taken from me, like the tent of a shepherd.
Præcisa est velut a texente vita mea;
My life has been cut off, as if by a weaver.
de mane usque ad vesperam finies me.
From morning until evening, you have marked out my limits.
so has he crushed all my bones.
de mane usque ad vesperam finies me.
From morning until evening, you have marked my limits.
My eyes have been weakened by gazing upward.
aut quid respondebit mihi, cum ipse fecerit?
or what would he answer me, since he himself has done this?
Recogitabo tibi omnes annos meos in amaritudine animæ meæ.
I will acknowledge to you all my years, in the bitterness of my soul.
et in talibus vita spiritus mei,
and if the life of my spirit is of such a kind,
and may you cause me to live.
Ecce in pace amaritudo mea amarissima.
Behold, in peace my bitterness is most bitter.
Tu autem eruisti animam meam ut non periret;
But you have rescued my soul, so that it would not perish.
projecisti post tergum tuum omnia peccata mea.
You have cast all my sins behind your back.
For Hell will not confess to you,
and death will not praise you.
non exspectabunt qui descendunt in lacum veritatem tuam.
Those who descend into the pit will not hope for your truth.
these will give praise to you,
as I also do this day!
pater filiis notam faciet veritatem tuam.
The father will make the truth known to the sons.
et psalmos nostros cantabimus cunctis diebus vitæ nostræ in domo Domini.
And we will sing our psalms, all the days of our life, in the house of the Lord.”
Et jussit Isaias ut tollerent massam de ficis,
Now Isaiah had ordered them to take a paste of figs,
and to spread it like plaster over the wound,
so that he would be healed.
Quod erit signum quia ascendam in domum Domini?
“What will be the sign that I may go up to the house of the Lord?”
